MechSwarm · codex art

Ten mutator faces, drawn in pixels

Every rule in the catalog, redrawn on a pixel grid at three canvas sizes — and shown at the sizes the game actually renders them: the 56px codex tile, the 28px deploy card, the 20px deploy chip.

The tint survives. These are not sprites. Each face is currentColor at three opacities — 1, 0.74, 0.42 — so a rule still wears its weight: Light, Heavy, Brutal. That is what killed the old PNG art; pixel art that carries its own palette would die the same way.

How they are drawn

One generator, one description per face, in unit coordinates. Primitives rasterise the way a pixel artist works — midpoint circles, integer scanline polygons, no antialiasing anywhere — so the same description lands on a 32 grid or a 128 grid, and detail passes switch on only where there is room for them.

A light pass runs last: every body pixel on the silhouette's top-left edge catches the light, every one on its bottom-right turns away. That is what makes these read as objects rather than as stencils, and it costs nothing but a third opacity.

Four faces changed shape in the process, because the pixel grid showed up problems the curves had hidden. Shield Towers was a dome on a plinth and read as a T-shirt — it is an arc over a flaring tower now. Armored Swarms had two rivets high on the shield that read as eyes; it has three studs on the seam instead. Amphibious' rising chevron reached the droplet's floor and cut a doorway, so the stem stops short. Hungry Mechs was given fangs and lost them again: a fang small enough to sit in the bite is four pixels of dirt at 20px.
